newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas edges up late on short covering.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas edges up late on short covering.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures edged higher late Monday in active trade, with short covering after a soft open lifing the complex despite slightly weaker physical prices, market sources said.

At 1350 EDT, August climbed 3.2 cents to $2.178 per million British thermal units after dipping early to $2.125. September was 5.9 cents higher at $2.155. Most other deferreds were steady to up by 3.8 cents.

"We dipped early on the (milder) weather, but everyone was waiting to buy $2.11 or $2.12 (basis August) and we never got there," said one Midwest trader, noting large open interest in August and shorts more pressed to cover ahead of the spot expiration Tuesday because of the physical premium to paper.
But some said they expected the rally to be tempered by the mostly mild Midwest and eastern weather expected this week which should trim demand.

Despite some heat today in the East, Weather Services expects temperatures there to cool tonight and remain below-normal for most of the rest of the week. Cooler Midwest weather also is forecast for the week, with Texas temperatures expected to drift around normal for the period.

Chart traders agreed August was caught in a range, with support still at $2.07 and then at the $2.051 low from July 8. Major trendline resistance was pegged at about $2.20. Further selling was likely at the $2.29 and $2.36 prominent highs.
Looking at September, support was seen at last week's low of $2.045. Resistance was seen first along the down trendline in the high-teens and then at $2.20.

In the cash Monday, Gulf Coast prices slipped several cents to the mid-teens, with gas at the Hub quoted in the high-teens. Midcon pipes were down a nickel at about the $2.10 level. New York city gate gas was flat to up slightly at $2.40-2.41.
NYMEX said 42,542 contracts traded at 1315 EDT. Hub open interest on July 25 rose 1,745 contracts to 209,976.
On the KCBT, August gained two cents to $2.115, while deferreds were steady to four cents higher. The East/West spread widened by 1.2 cents to 6.3 cents (NYMEX premium).
